remaining_gaps.topic: Spirits May Yet Dream previews a Fear Card without earning it or accelerating resolution
remaining_gaps.proposed_question: Bringer uses Spirits May Yet Dream to turn an unearned Fear Card in the Fear deck face-up. Does turning it face-up immediately earn that card or let players resolve its Fear effect now, or must it still be earned and resolved normally?

predetermined_answer.answer: Turning it face-up only previews the card. It does not earn it or resolve its effect. The card is still earned and resolved normally, with its Fear effect waiting for the ordinary Fear resolution procedure after it is earned.
minimum_asked_facts: Turning the card face-up does not itself earn the card.
Turning it face-up does not resolve its Fear effect or grant early resolution; normal earning and resolution still apply.
no_extra_grading_requirements: No arbitrary Fear-marker count, card identity, deck depth, threshold numerical recall, or complete Fear-step recital is required.
Do not require restating current Terror rules or a victory check not asked.

primary_sources.transcription: Turn any face-down Fear Card face-up. (It’s earned/resolved normally, but players can see what’s coming.)

literal_asks.Q87: Can Spirits May Yet Dream flip a Fear Card already earned, on top of the deck or deeper in the deck?
literal_asks.Q11: In a two-Spirit game with 7 of 8 Fear markers already generated, an effect generates 3 Fear and earning a card exposes Terror II. Explain marker handling, new Terror timing, and when the card is revealed/resolved.
literal_asks.Q139: Three Fear Cards were earned in a known order. During the Fear step, may players inspect all three before resolving the first? In which order are they resolved, and where does each card go once resolved?
literal_asks.Q168: When Spirits May Yet Dream grants its target an Element, may that Spirit choose an Element it currently has none of, or must the chosen Element already be present?

actual_prompt_overlap_assessment.assessment: Q87 asks only whether the first effect may flip cards in three locations; a yes correctly answers it without stating what flipping does to earning or resolution. Q168 asks the separate Element-eligibility instruction. Q11 asks ordinary marker/earning/Terror/reveal timing, without this native preview intervention; Q139 asks ordinary already-earned stack inspection/order/discard. Correct answers to all four can coexist with the false belief that this special innate also earns or resolves its chosen card. No other literal prompt asks what flipping with this innate does to earning or resolution.

remaining_gaps.why_novel: The printed parenthetical explicitly defines the procedural boundary of an information-revealing exception: visibility changes while earning and resolution do not. This is the scope of a named original innate permission, not another card name, numeric payload, target/distance variant or a newly invented combination. The gap does not ask every printed card effect; it isolates an explicit source-defined timing/earning branch not requested by the existing location-eligibility ask.
